text: History before the seal. Both constants (DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_INITIAL_READ_TIMEOUT_MS = 300, DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_CONTROLLER_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 300) were introduced by 9939b3ff6 (2026-02-24, 'node orchestration hardening') and never changed; src/config/dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js was last touched by 54dd2d7ce (2026-10-27), 8a2bd2b44, 06273547c and b1acc899f, none changing the bounds or their fallback. The bounded-wait census of 2026-10-04 (solve/epics/raft-rs-full-cutover/census-bounded-waits-2026-10-04.md lines 114 and 442-443) classified both as startup time-boxes with a designed fallback, 'Defaults apply now and CDC applies the stored values later', fallthrough_alternative, warn, and test/config/dynamic-config-startup-wait-bound-spent.test.js witnesses that classification (an expired box logs INITIAL_APPLY_FAILED, never wait_bound_spent, and startup proceeds). No other quest names dynamic-config startup (grep of solve/quests and solve/epics: only the two censuses, the f1-step-down-port static investigation and the system-table-write-admission design mention the wiring). New evidence against the designed fallback: the wiring applies a late value only through handleCdcApplied on CDC_APPLIED events for the config table (dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js 451-477), so a stored value already local with no later CDC apply (a restarting node) is never applied; and the spent controller bound orphans a live RaftAdaptiveTimingController (withTimeout 76-107 never cancels; the reference is dropped 438-449; initialize, registerWatchers and startLoop continue; shutdown 492-501 shuts only the controller held). The seal supersedes the 2026-10-04 classification explicitly (R09) and requires the witness test to be re-derived, not deleted (ruling of the lead).

seal.statement: src/config/dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js is the one owner of the node's startup dynamic configuration, rows 4 and 5 of the fixed-work-bound census (the same wiring owns both, so they are one quest). When the 300 ms startup bound DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_INITIAL_READ_TIMEOUT_MS is spent, the late value of that key is still applied, by the same owner, whether it arrives by the completed read or by a CDC apply of the config table: a stored value already local with no later CDC apply (a restarting node) is applied when its read completes, never silently left at the default. When DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_CONTROLLER_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS is spent, the in-flight RaftAdaptiveTimingController.initialize() is never orphaned: the controller either becomes owned when it completes (then shut down by the wiring's shutdown) or is cancelled and shut down, never both, never a second controller beside it, with a typed startup outcome recorded either way. Under R09 this supersedes, explicitly, the designed-fallback classification of both 300 ms boxes recorded by the bounded-wait census of 2026-10-04 (solve/epics/raft-rs-full-cutover/census-bounded-waits-2026-10-04.md lines 114, 442-443: 'Defaults apply now and CDC applies the stored values later') and witnessed by test/config/dynamic-config-startup-wait-bound-spent.test.js: new evidence shows the late value is applied only through handleCdcApplied on CDC_APPLIED events for the config table (dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js 451-477), so a value with no later CDC apply is never applied, and the spent controller bound orphans a live controller (withTimeout 76-107 never cancels; the wiring drops its reference 438-449; initialize, registerWatchers and the loop continue; shutdown 492-501 only shuts the controller it holds). That witness test is re-derived to the new contract, never deleted. Startup still never blocks on the bounds.

text: Red first, before any src change: test/config/dynamic-config-startup-owned-initialization.test.js (config reads that answer only after 700 ms, longer than the 300 ms read bound and the controller's own 300 ms bound, which starts after the reads). Row 4: a restarting node's stored raft timing (heartbeat 120, election 1800-5400, tick 25), no CDC apply: the replicas end on the defaults (heartbeat 50), never the stored values (not ok at the behavioural same()). Row 5: raft.adaptiveTimingEnabled stored true: the orphaned controller's initialize completes after the bound and starts its loop; after wiring.shutdown() its interval is still alive (not ok at intervals.live.size === 0). The existing witnesses stay green at the base: dynamic-config-startup-wiring.test.js 38 assertions, dynamic-config-startup-wait-bound-spent.test.js 25 (evidence/red-before-fix.log.txt).

Attempt 1 under the lead's go. src/config/dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js owns every piece of startup work it starts: withTimeout (which rejected and abandoned) is replaced by waitWithinBound, which waits for owned work up to the bound without abandoning it (timer unref'd and cleared by settle or shutdown). Each spent bound is a reported late state: reportWaitBoundSpent under the constant's own name (DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_INITIAL_READ_TIMEOUT_MS per key, DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_CONTROLLER_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS), closing the census's visibility gap for rows 4 and 5; bounds keep their values. Startup proceeds on the defaults as before. Row 4: every read result, on time or late, goes through one apply path (applyStartupValue: a logging key applies at once; a raft key joins the startup sweep while it has not run, and applies its own sweep after it); ordering rule: the CDC_APPLIED listener is subscribed before any read starts and counts applies of the config table per key; a late read whose key was CDC-applied since it started is dropped as stale (the CDC value wins), so each key's read applies at most once. Row 5: the wiring holds the one controller reference from construction to shutdown, never dropped; a late initialize completes into the same on-time path (the controller starts its own loop if enabled) and is recorded adopted_late; shutdown always stops the controller, and src/config/raft-adaptive-timing-controller.js initialize now checks a stopped flag after each await before registering watchers, detecting the profile or starting the loop (startLoop also refuses when stopped), so a shutdown during initialize cancels the rest. Why no work can neither complete nor cancel: the reference is never dropped, shutdown is unconditional, and initialize has no side effect after a stop. Typed outcomes (DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_OUTCOME: pending, applied, applied_late, dropped_stale, failed, cancelled, adopted_late, unavailable) via wiring.startupOutcome(). test/config/dynamic-config-startup-wait-bound-spent.test.js re-derived (not deleted). Tests: the row-4 and row-5 witnesses (red before, green now), plus row-4 ordering (CDC wins, exactly once) and row-5 cancellation (shutdown during initialize: no loop, no watcher); five mutations each red; lane 8 files pass=8 assertions=870 with LAGRANGE_PLACEMENT=local; test:static clean after the metadata refresh (one unused-export fixed by importing the outcome constant in the test). CHANGELOG entry. Decision under R16 (lead's ruling on F3): scope widened to src/config/dynamic-config-service.js. The service cache owns the value, so ordering is fixed there: the per-key CDC apply sequence lives in the service (cdcApplySequence), get() does not write a read that a later CDC apply overtook, and the wiring's staleness check asks the same sequence, so one owner decides. Pre-existing at base, reached by this quest's late reads.

CDC shape and replay. Measured (test/config/dynamic-config-cdc-update-shape.test.js, real PartitionCDCGenerator, real system-table UPDATE SQL, better-sqlite3): the committed UPDATE's event data carries config_key, from the fetched row, and from the WHERE parameters when the row is gone. So CDC-wins is not inert. Read, not measured: the message-group paths copy data unchanged to cdcApplied (message-group-service-cdc-propagation-runtime-methods.js 312-321, message-group-service-raft-timing.js 38-50). replayOnly: a delivery-profile flag only (cdc-propagation-delivery-profile.js 266, partition-cdc-delivery.js 110-115); it suppresses neither apply nor cdcApplied; measured at the service, a replay-only event is counted and applied as any other. Trace of restart: the applied path gates emission on the cdcHandler LWW result, the committed path (raft-timing 38-50) does not, and DynamicConfigService has no LWW of its own, so the last arrival wins. An older committed entry re-applied in log order would transiently regress the value and bump the sequence, and it ends on the log's last entry. Not measured: a real restart replay, and whether a live restart re-applies entries after the wiring subscribes. No distributed run.

F4 disclosure, correcting the ruling's wording after reading the certifier: the two constants are now known findings owned by this quest, with the reason that late is a reported state and startup proceeds non-blocking; the 2026-10-04 no-longer-emitted list is corrected under R09; the CHANGELOG says they emit. This keeps them visible, but it does NOT make them non-failing. CERTIFICATION_KNOWN_FINDING_SPENT_WAIT_POLICY is FAIL (scenario-certification.js 147-148, asserted by its test at 667), so a certification run with a spend still fails, as certification_known_finding_spent_wait with the owner named, instead of certification_unexpected_spent_wait. Only the owner relaxes that policy, and it is unchanged here. For Peter: at this quest's head a spent 300 ms startup bound blocks certification, as it would have at the earlier attempt under another failure name. At base the bounds did not reach the certifier as spent waits, per the census list.

R17, not fixed here (verifier's F7-F10, plus one found in the corrective): F7 a read that never settles stays pending in startupOutcome after shutdown. F8 RaftAdaptiveTimingController.loadConfig keeps reading after stop. F9 late raft keys sweep per key, so replicas can pass through a mixed timing set while keys arrive. F10 an evaluateOnce in flight at shutdown is not awaited. New: a value that a sweep refuses stays in the wiring's working timing set, so until it becomes valid a later valid CDC of another key is refused too; the CDC watcher already behaved this way for an invalid CDC value; rolling back instead would lose a stored pair that is only valid together, which is witnessed. F11 is fixed: LATE_READ_DROPPED_STALE is now STARTUP_READ_SUPERSEDED_BY_CDC, since the read need not be late.

Corrective attempt for the rejection of 791bd628a (R1). A refused or waiting raft value leaves the working timing set for a separate held map. Each sweep tries working plus held; if refused and a CDC key changed, it sweeps working with that key alone and keeps the values held. One path for on-time and late (R11), covering B1 to B4. Heal: when the wiring holds a failed or refused key, a CDC for that key is adopted even if the value equals the service cache; new outcome healed_by_cdc; a failed read is not retried and its warning says so, no retry loop. A held refused outcome clears when that key's own CDC resolves it. A refused CDC value goes to held too.
